claims.text: For \(v=v_{r,s,t,n}\) with \(\mathfrak S_v=s_{i^j}\), \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\), the two sets \[ \{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\},\qquad \{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\} \] generate \(J_v\subseteq H^\star(G/P_J,\mathbb Z)\cong\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\); each has \(N=\binom{a+b}{a}\) elements. 1382:   Given a bigrassmannian $v=v_{r,s,t,n}$ in type $A_{n-1}$ with $\schubp_v = s_{i^j}$, let
1383: $$
1384: \begin{aligned}
1385: a&:=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\\
1386: b&:=\min(i,j).
1387: \end{aligned}
1388: $$
1389: 
1390: Then $J_v$ is generated as an ideal of 
1391: $H^{\star}(G/P_J, {\mathbb Z})\cong \Lambda/I_{r,n-r}$ by 
1392: \begin{equation}
1393: \label{generating-set-one}
1394: \{ s_{\mu}: i^j \subseteq \mu \subseteq ((i+a)^b,i^{j-b}) \}.
1395: \end{equation}
1396: 
1397: Alternatively, $J_v$ is generated by 
1398: \begin{equation}
1399: \label{generating-set-two}
1400: \{ s_{\mu}: i^j \subseteq \mu \subseteq (i^j,b^a) \}.
1401: \end{equation}
1402: \end{theorem}
1403: 
1404: We delay our proof of Theorem~\ref{J-generators} until Section~\ref{minconjsection}.
1405: 
1406: \noindent
1407: Note that in both of the asserted generating sets \eqref{generating-set-one} and \eqref{generating-set-two} for $J_v$,
1408: the shapes $\mu$ indexing the generators $s_\mu$ run through an interval between
1409: the $j \times i$ rectangular shape $i^j$ and the disjoint union of $i^j$ with a 
1410: smaller rectangle of shape $a \times b$ or $b \times a$. 
1411: In \eqref{generating-set-one} the smaller rectangle is to the right
1412: of the rectangle $i^j$, with both top-justified, while in \eqref{generating-set-two} the 
1413: smaller rectangle is below the rectangle $i^j$, with both left-justified.  
1414: Thus in both cases, the generating sets have size $\binom{a+b}{a}$
1415: and consist of generators whose multiset of degrees
1416: have generating function 
1417: $$
1418: \sum_\mu q^{|\mu|} = q^{ij} \qbin{a+b}{a},
1419: $$
1420: where $\qbin{a+b}{a}$ is a $q$-{\it binomial coefficient} or {\it Gaussian polynomial} 
1421: \cite[I.2 Exer. 3]{Macdonald}.

claims.text: The paper conjectures that both sets are minimal and reports computer verification only for \(r\le4\) and \(n-r\le5\). [source-2@L1489-L1502|claim=formal-document]

The paper applies its graded proposition with \(\Lambda\) the graded ring of symmetric functions over \(\mathbb Z\), \(M=J_v\), and explicitly leaves unresolved whether \(M/\Lambda_+M\) requires \(N\) generators or is \(\mathbb Z^N\). [source-2@L1517-L1552|claim=formal-document]

claims.text: **Indexed graded Nakayama.** Let \(R\) be commutative unital, \(\Lambda=\bigoplus_{e\ge0}\Lambda_e\) a connected graded \(R\)-algebra with \(\Lambda_0=R\), and \(M=\bigoplus_{d\ge d_0}M_d\) a bounded-below graded \(\Lambda\)-module. For any indexed homogeneous family \((m_\alpha)_{\alpha\in A}\), it generates \(M\) iff \((\bar m_\alpha)_{\alpha\in A}\) spans \(Q:=M/\Lambda_+M\) over \(R\). Indeed, the forward direction is immediate. Conversely, induct on \(d\). For \(x\in M_d\), gradedness gives \[ x-\sum_{\alpha\in F,\ \deg m_\alpha=d}r_\alpha m_\alpha\in(\Lambda_+M)_d =\sum_{e>0}\Lambda_eM_{d-e}, \] for a finite \(F\subset A\). Every latter module factor has degree \(<d\), hence belongs to the generated submodule by induction.

Under the hypotheses above, the family \((m_\alpha)\) is inclusion-minimal precisely when \((\bar m_\alpha)\) is an inclusion-minimal \(R\)-spanning family of \(Q\): apply indexed graded Nakayama to every subfamily obtained by deleting one index.

If \(A=\Lambda/I\), \(J\subseteq A\) is an ideal, and \(S\subseteq J\), then \(S\) generates \(J\) as an \(A\)-ideal iff it generates \(J\) as a \(\Lambda\)-module. Thus the preceding criterion applies to \(J_v\).

An exact sufficient hypothesis for either displayed \(N\)-element Schur family to be irredundant is \[ \mu_{\mathbb Z}\!\left(J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\right)=N. \] It spans the quotient by graded Nakayama; deletion would give a spanning family of \(N-1\) elements, contradicting the hypothesis.

A stronger sufficient hypothesis is \[ J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\cong\mathbb Z^N. \] An \(N\)-element spanning family of \(\mathbb Z^N\) cannot remain spanning after a deletion, since \(\mathbb Z^{N-1}\) cannot surject onto \(\mathbb Z^N\).

**Free-summand irredundance construction.** If \(R\ne0\), \(Q=R^d\oplus T\), and \(t_1,\ldots,t_k\) is an inclusion-minimal spanning family of \(T\), then \[ \{(e_\ell,0):1\le\ell\le d\}\ \cup\ \{(0,t_j):1\le j\le k\} \] is an inclusion-minimal spanning family of \(Q\). Coordinate projections witness necessity of the first \(d\) elements, and \(Q\to T\) witnesses necessity of the others.

**CRT-aligned construction.** Let \(n_1,\ldots,n_k>1\) be pairwise coprime, \(M=\prod_i n_i\), and \(T=\mathbb Z/M\). Choose \(c_i\) with \(c_i(M/n_i)\equiv1\pmod {n_i}\), and put \(\epsilon_i=c_iM/n_i\bmod M\). Under \[ T\cong\bigoplus_{i=1}^k\mathbb Z/n_i, \] \(\epsilon_i\) is the \(i\)-th coordinate unit. Hence \(\{\epsilon_1,\ldots,\epsilon_k\}\) is inclusion-minimal spanning, while \(\{1\}\) is also inclusion-minimal spanning.

Claim 9 is correct: in \(\mathbb Z/6\), \(\{1\}\) generates, while \(\{2,3\}\) generates because \(1=2\cdot2-3\), and neither singleton \(\{2\}\) nor \(\{3\}\) generates. Thus both are inclusion-minimal, of cardinalities \(1\) and \(2\). More generally, adjoining the free summand \(\mathbb Z^d\) to the CRT construction gives irredundant spanning families of \(\mathbb Z^d\oplus\mathbb Z/M\) of sizes \(d+1\) and \(d+k\).

No supplied evidence proves \(\mu_{\mathbb Z}(J_v/\Lambda_+J_v)=\binom{a+b}{a}\), torsion-freeness of this quotient, or the source’s stronger \(\mathbb Z^N\) formulation; consequently the minimality conjecture for \(J_v\) remains unresolved.
